articles.title: ‘No negativity’: Carrick still confident at Manchester United despite ‘sticky’ start
articles.summary: United have endured worst league start since 1986-87. Trip to Atlético in Champions League awaits on Tuesday. Manchester United have endured their worst league start in 40 years but Michael Carrick insists he is “loving it”.
body: Despite collecting just six points in the Premier League so far, Carrick claimed he did not feel under pressure and backed his captain, Bruno Fernandes, who he revealed was still “carrying something”, to rediscover his form. As he talked about building, there was a reminder too of the fact that Arsenal, the champions, finished “seventh or eighth” in Mikel Arteta’s first two seasons.

“To do something good, to do something great, you have got to be able to do something difficult,” said Carrick, whose side take on Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano Stadium in the second round of games in the Champions League league phase on Tuesday.

articles.title: 49ers’ Dre Greenlaw suspended after headbutt leaves opponent bleeding
articles.summary: Ernest Jones IV was not wearing helmet during incident. Linebacker will miss game against Commanders. San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw was suspended for one game after headbutting Seattle’s Ernest Jones IV in the wake of a late hit on the Seahawks sideline.
body: The NFL issued the suspension on Monday, saying the headbutt of a player without a helmet during Sunday’s 32-29 win against Seattle was “contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.”
Greenlaw will miss San Francisco’s game next Monday night against Washington, although he can appeal his punishment.
Sunday’s incident came when Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold scrambled and was hit late by Greenlaw after going out of bounds, leading to a personal foul in a game San Francisco went on to win 32-29.
Several Seahawks defenders immediately confronted Greenlaw after the hit and the linebacker responded by headbutting Jones. Jones was bleeding after the hit and Greenlaw was ejected.

articles.title: Christian Horner: ‘Not all teams act that way. You don’t see the same brutality as when I left’
articles.summary: The 52-year-old reflects on the pain of being sacked after two decades turning Red Bull into an F1 powerhouse, questioning his purpose in life and dealing with panic attacks.
body: Christian Horner should be in steamy Singapore, preparing for another grand prix victory, but here he is, at home on an autumnal morning in genteel Highgate as his wife, Geri Halliwell-Horner, welcomes me with a cheerful hug. Horner smiles as the former Spice Girl produces an impressive imitation of my South African accent which echoes her old headteacher at Watford Girls.

After the most controversial man in the recent history of Formula One says hello, Halliwell-Horner and I discuss the fact that my two daughters also went to her school and that one of their history textbooks had her name printed on the inside page – while the ex-Ginger Spice talks about gritty old Watford, grammar school education and Nelson Mandela.

I joke that it feels like I’m interviewing Halliwell-Horner instead of Horner. Everyone laughs but I will soon ask Horner about the impact on his marriage in 2024 when an investigation was carried out into allegations he had sent “hundreds” of inappropriate texts and photographs to a female employee when Red Bull’s team principal. The woman was apparently “upset, angry, scared, intimidated and lonely” while the tabloids speculated that Halliwell-Horner was “furious”.

articles.title: Price rules out Shields but hints at big fight in 2027
articles.summary: Lauren Price will fight Michaela Kotaskova in Cardiff in November with "exciting" plans for early 2027, but rules out facing American star Claressa Shields.
body: Lauren Price is eyeing a fight that will be "massive for world boxing" if she can overcome Michaela Kotaskova next month - but has ruled out facing Claressa Shields for now.
Olympic gold medallist Price will put her unified WBA, WBC and IBF welterweight titles on the line when she fights the Czech at Cardiff's Utilita Arena on 20 November.

The bout, which will be shown live on the BBC, will be Price's first since a gruelling title defence against Stephanie Pineiro in April, which had undisputed heavyweight champion Shields watching on in attendance.
It had been thought the pair would meet at middleweight but Price says talks broke down.

articles.title: Man City bananas 'brought fun back', says Varadi
articles.summary: Former Manchester City striker Imre Varadi says it was "brilliant to see" the club's fans waving inflatable bananas at Anfield and feels it "brought a lot of fun back".
body: Former Manchester City striker Imre Varadi said it was "brilliant to see" the club's fans waving inflatable bananas at Anfield on Sunday and feels it "brought a lot of fun back".

Varadi was nicknamed 'Imre Banana' by City fans during his two-year spell with the club in the late 1980s and they began taking inflatable bananas to games when they played in the old Second Division.
The craze continued into the early 90s, with City fans taking bananas to games intermittently since, and dozens re-emerged at Sunday's game.
City's 3-0 win over Liverpool was the club's first game since being found guilty of 114 charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

articles.title: UH football notes: Patrick Overmyer, Liam Dougherty earn Big 12 accolades
articles.summary: A pair of record-setting performances by the University of Houston earned Big 12 honors Monday. Tight end Patrick Overmyer was named offensive player of the week, and punter Liam Dougherty was selected special teams player of the week, the Big 12 announced.
body: Overmyer tied an FBS record for touchdown receptions by a tight end with four in Saturday's 35-16 win at Kansas State.
Halfway through the regular season, Overmyer leads all tight ends nationally with six touchdown receptions and is second in receptions (33) and receiving yards (393).

"It's awesome," Overmyer said after becoming the seventh tight end with four touchdowns in a game in FBS history. "But I just want to say thank you to my coaches and my team. They're the ones that put me in that opportunity, and I was lucky enough to be there when my name was called. So credit goes to them."
Dougherty averaged 59.3 yards on three punts, surpassing the previous school record of 55.3 yards set by Jimmy McClary against Louisville in 2003.

articles.title: GB's Richardson withdrawn from World Championships
articles.summary: Matt Richardson is withdrawn from the Great Britain squad for next week's World Track Cycling Championships amid reports he is under investigation for misconduct.
body: British Cycling confirmed the 27-year-old Olympic medallist's removal in a statement but did not give a reason.
When approached by BBC Sport, British Cycling declined to comment on allegations first reported by The Times, external it was because of a misconduct investigation.
Last Wednesday, Richardson was named in the British squad for the championships, which run from 14-18 October.
He had been expected to contend for three medals in the team sprint, individual sprint and keirin.

articles.title: Stroppa on Venezia future: ‘You shouldn’t ask me’ as Zanetti and Nicola circle
articles.summary: Giovanni Stroppa’s future at Venezia hangs in the balance after Monday’s 3-1 defeat to Atalanta left the Lagunari without a point after six Serie A games. As noted by FirenzeViola, the club could give Stroppa one last chance against Napoli, but Paolo Zanetti and Davide Nicola are already being…
body: Stroppa led Venezia back to Serie A as Serie B champions last season, and he insisted his side deserve far more than their results suggest.

“Trust? You shouldn’t ask me,” he told DAZN. “The results are penalising us. I work for what I can give the team, and they look very lively to me. We’re getting important players back. I think I’ve done my job to the best of my ability, and I take full responsibility. I see how the team works, and it deserves much more.”

Zanetti knows the club well, having led Venezia to promotion in 2021, and Sportitalia reports that his assistant was in the stands in Bergamo. Nicola, known for his relegation escapes, has also been linked, as reported by Tuttomercatoweb.
Venezia were 2-0 down inside six minutes and 3-1 behind at the break, but they produced a strong second half, hitting the woodwork twice and having a goal disallowed for offside.

articles.summary: Mensur Suljovic's crowd incitement during his match against Ross Smith and his alleged sexist comments in his on-stage interview regarding the incident have been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority.
body: The Austrian encouraged the crowd to boo the Englishman during a last-leg decider in their third-round clash at the Swiss Darts Trophy on Sunday afternoon.
He was later asked about the incident in an on-stage interview and used an allegedly sexist comment to describe how Smith reacted.
Suljovic said: "Ross Smith is one of the best players in the world - what's the bloke complaining about? He's got to play his game; otherwise, he's welcome to go home.
"Women, women - they're always complaining, sorry. Sorry, you don't do that. I fully accept him as one of the very best darts players.

articles.title: Four Super League clubs show support for NRL deal after Leigh criticism
articles.summary: Leeds Rhinos, St Helens, Hull KR and Hull FC have released statements in favour of the NRL's investment in Super League after Leigh Leopards owner Derek Beaumont came out against the deal on social media.
body: Talks have been ongoing for months regarding the Australian competition's potential future involvement in Super League to bring alignment between the top two rugby league competitions in the world.

As a requirement of the deal, it is understood the NRL would want London Broncos added to the top flight as the 15th team from the 2027 season onwards which has been a potential sticking point for some clubs, with Leigh Leopards owner Derek Beaumont taking to social media to say he is against the deal because of that particular point.
Beaumont said it is "just not right to put London in Super League".
The Leigh owner's particular grievance is that London finished 16th in the gradings, outside of the automatic Super League spots.
